C-ARCHIVE-CORPUS-BASELINE-1-0AA78642.Summary: Narrow the attempt-pair archive-corpus regression in `src/review/core.test.ts` from an unconditional zero over every dynamically enumerated archive bundle to (a) a frozen zero over the verified 27-bundle historical close membership plus (b) a retired-code-only zero over the complete current archive. Add the additive `bun run validate:ci` entry to `.ngrace-lint.json` `closeEvidenceCommandShapes` so the mandated post-archive whole-CI criterion is warning-clean and discriminating. No runtime, catalogue, skill, workflow, packaging, version, or old-archive change. This is corrective work for the failing CI on branch `feat/retire-declaration-guard`.

Goals.Goal: Restore the CI suite to green on `feat/retire-declaration-guard` by scoping the corpus regression to the verified historical close membership while keeping the retired-code rejection over the complete current archive.

Make the post-archive whole-CI run (`bun run validate:ci`) a close-bound criterion evaluated in the applied-archive state, including this bundle's own archive arrival, so the failure the predecessor's pre-archive-only validation missed cannot recur.

Constraints.Constraint: The only file changed under `src/` is the test file `src/review/core.test.ts`; its runtime module owner is `M-REVIEW`, taken from `src/review/core.ts`'s `LINKS` header. `src/review/core.ts` and `src/review/catalog.ts` are byte-identical to base `f346480034693efde289eb65920be1832d88d189`; no skill, workflow, packaging, version, OpenPackage, plugin, or old-archive file changes. `.ngrace-lint.json` gains exactly one additive `closeEvidenceCommandShapes` entry, `"bun run validate:ci"`, because that command matches no default discriminating CloseEvidence shape and the lint engine's own remediation (`change.close-evidence-undiscriminating`) names the config prefix as the remedy. The entry is additive; it removes no default command shape and changes no other key or value. `.ngrace-lint.json` and `.test.ts` files are not module-ownable write paths, so no synthetic `LINKS:` header or new graph anchor is added for either.

Historical membership is the verified 27-bundle close membership: the existing 26 `AUTHORING_ARCHIVE_C_IDS` (authoring-time constant at `src/review/core.test.ts:1767-1794`) plus the authoring bundle `C-SUBSTANTIATION-HONESTY`. It is verified against historical close commit `20b9135b47771b66efebe40709dd7c777936d901` at authoring time and embedded as a constant in the regression. The regression asserts every historical member still exists as a `C-*` directory under `.ngrace/changes/archive/`. It must not assert that today's complete archive contains exactly 27 members. The test consumes only the embedded list and the working tree and requires no historical git object at runtime; full-history CI checkout is not restored.

This overturns D0's ongoing dynamic-zero mechanism (`.ngrace/changes/archive/C-SUBSTANTIATION-HONESTY/plan.xml:157-195`), which widened the spec's 26-bundle zero (`C-SUBSTANTIATION-HONESTY/spec.xml:404-423`, `AC-ARCHIVE-CORPUS-ZERO`) to every dynamically enumerated archive bundle. D0's original counterweight was prevention of denominator shrink — a silently vanished bundle could not shrink the set being checked. The frozen historical membership plus the required presence check preserves that counterweight without promising zero live findings over every future delivery. The complete current archive is still enumerated, but only the retired code `review.attempt-pair-unsubstantiated` is required to be absent everywhere.

The retained live finding on `C-DECLARATION-GUARD-RETIRE-1-C69B6AB6` (T-005 events 14→15, id `792aa42b0c989c73`) is acknowledged but remains detected. Its immutable run events are not rewritten, no code suppresses the detector, and the historical bound pass's Ack is not transferred to today's different whole snapshot (acks are bound to a change id, snapshot digest, and finding id; `C-BOUND-VERDICT/spec.xml:430-530`). C-ARCHIVE-CORPUS-BASELINE-1-0AA78642.Problem:
CI on branch `feat/retire-declaration-guard` fails the test `archive corpus: zero live and retired findings on every dynamically enumerated C-*` at `src/review/core.test.ts:2004`. CI reported 2,478 pass, 6 skip, 1 fail, and `validate:ci` exited 1; the Windows and Dart jobs passed. The test grew an over-broad assertion from D0's plan-level widening: the spec's `AC-ARCHIVE-CORPUS-ZERO` (`C-SUBSTANTIATION-HONESTY/spec.xml:404-423`) pinned zero over 26 authoring bundles, and D0 (`C-SUBSTANTIATION-HONESTY/plan.xml:157-195`) widened that to a dynamic enumeration of the whole archive, asserting zero live findings on every enumerated bundle. That widening was correct for its original counterweight — it caught a silent vanish by enumerating dynamically and asserting presence of a frozen authoring set — but it silently converted the zero into a promise over every future delivery.
The promise now fails for a legitimate, retained result. Whole-population measurement on 2026-10-01 found 163 direct `C-*` archive directories, one live attempt-pair finding, and zero retired-code findings. The sole live finding is on `C-DECLARATION-GUARD-RETIRE-1-C69B6AB6`, T-005 events 14→15, id `792aa42b0c989c73`. The chronology claim for that pair was withdrawn and the finding acknowledged, but the immutable attempt events remain and the detector correctly still raises. The current full review has four findings; the latest historical bound pass has nineteen, and its Ack is bound to that historical snapshot, not to today's different whole snapshot, so it does not clear this finding.
The historical close commit `20b9135b47771b66efebe40709dd7c777936d901` contains exactly 27 archive bundles: the 26 `AUTHORING_ARCHIVE_C_IDS` plus `C-SUBSTANTIATION-HONESTY` itself. A fresh rescore of all 27 yields zero live and zero retired findings, and the five existing positive/F286 fixtures pass. That is the verified historical baseline this change freezes.
The predecessor `C-DECLARATION-GUARD-RETIRE-1-C69B6AB6` ran the full `bun run validate:ci` `MustPassCommand` only before apply/archive (`plan.xml:37-44`) and its post-archive verdict ran only focused commands (`spec.xml:473-480`), explicitly never rerunning the root suite or `validate:ci`. Because the archive-corpus test enumerates the archive, the pre-archive run did not see the bundle's own arrival, and the post-archive focused checks omitted the suite that would have caught it. This change therefore keeps a frozen zero over the verified historical membership, keeps the retired-code rejection over the complete archive, and adds a post-archive whole-suite criterion so the same gap cannot recur.
